question: Is a lineage's overall phylogenetic-memory level related to how closely its within-lineage trait ordering follows the global trait prior?

definitions.memory_level: family BLUP from rho ~ 0 + trait_name + (1|family) on cleaned/matched log S3 effects
definitions.allocation_disagreement: within each family, fraction of non-tied trait-pair comparisons whose observed order disagrees with leave-one-family-out global trait means
definitions.allocation_alignment: Spearman correlation, within a family, between observed trait rho and leave-one-family-out global trait means when at least 3 traits are available

interpretation: Overall lineage-wide memory level and trait-specific allocation of memory are empirically decoupled in both compilations. A family can show high or low average phylogenetic memory without being more or less faithful to the global trait ordering.
conceptual_model: Lineage context has at least two separable dimensions: a scalar memory-level shift F_f and a trait-allocation/re-ordering component U_ft.
hard_nonclaims: This post-outcome analysis does not identify a mechanism.
Null correlation does not prove exact statistical independence.
Family BLUP and allocation metrics are estimated with unequal precision among families.
